title: SRE Oncall Scratchpad - 2026-03-19
content:
Summary / context:
- Oncall shift 08:00-20:00 PT. Primary pager coverage for serving runtime and infra.
- Night: brief increased 500 errors on hosted-api around 02:20 PT (see JIRA-4820). Root cause: partial Redis cluster flapping after control-plane deploy. Mitigated by auto-failover and rolling restart; system recovered ~02:37.
- Morning stability check at shift start: CPU/GPU clusters healthy; a few transient KV cache misses but within expected.

Incidents yesterday (quick notes):
- JIRA-4820 (500s on hosted-api):
  - Timeline: 02:15 alert -> 02:18 spike -> 02:25 paging escalated to SRE -> 02:30 failover started -> 02:37 service recovered.
  - Steps taken: triggered redis failover (manual trigger to ensure clean primary), restarted control-plane deployment replica that failed liveness probe, increased connection drain-delay for subsequent deploys.
  - Follow-ups: add liveness probe tolerance for control-plane pods (PR open: ops#128). Add alert to detect cross-az replication lag early.
  - Owner: Noah Chen (follow-up on infra changes).

Open follow-ups / TODOs (priority ordered):
1) Runbook updates for redis failover (owners: Alexis + Noah) - add exact recovery commands, expected RTO, verification steps, and a snippet to rollback recent control-plane deploys. (Due: 2026-03-23)
2) Alert tuning: split 500-series alerts by error type (client vs server), add replication-lag metric threshold for redis cluster. (Owner: Harper)
3) Post-incident blameless writeup draft in Confluence (link above) - include timeline, mitigations, proposed infra changes. (Owner: Alexis)
4) Add canary gating to control-plane deploys to avoid multi-az liveness cascades. Draft proposal in ops repo. (Owner: platform-eng)
5) Run a small chaos test against redis replicas next week to validate failover automation (Owner: eng-sre).

Notes to self - command snippets and checks:
- Check redis replication lag:
  kubectl exec -it redis-primary-0 -- redis-cli INFO replication | egrep "role|master_repl_offset|slave_repl_offset"
- Force failover (if needed):
  redis-cli -h <replica-host> -p <port> CLUSTER FAILOVER force
- Check control-plane pods and liveness events:
  kubectl -n control-plane get pods -o wide --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
  kubectl -n control-plane describe pod <pod> | egrep "Liveness|RestartCount|Events" -A3

Monitoring checks at start of shift:
- grafana: serving-runtime overview dashboard - check 1m P50/P95 latency, request rate, error rate.
- infra: redis cluster health, cross-az replication lag, node CPU/mem.
- autoscaler: confirm no recent failed scale events in last 6h.
- cost alerts: none fired overnight.

Quick observations / small annoyances:
- Some dashboards still use old label key `env=prod` vs `environment=prod` (causes missing panels when switching queries). Flag for dashboard cleanup (tickets on backlog).
- Console traces for the 02:20 incident had truncated logs due to rlog rotation config - raise to infra to bump rotation size.

Hand-off notes for next oncall (Harper):
- Watch for residual JIRA-4820 follow-ups; Noah will be pushing infra PRs today.
- If 500s re-appear, check redis replication metrics first (grafana panel: infra -> redis -> repl-lag) then control-plane deploy events. Avoid immediate full restart of control-plane; try targeted replica restart first.
- Contact list: Noah Chen (infra lead), Priya Shah (platform-eng), Emma Sullivan (sre). Pager: #sre-oncall Slack.

Unresolved questions / decisions needed:
- Should we increase livenessProbe.failureThreshold for control-plane pods from 3->6? (tradeoff: slower detection vs fewer false restarts). Need agreement from platform-eng.
- Do we add canary gating to all control-plane deployments or just cross-az ones? Drafting options in ops PR.

Misc TODO (low priority):
- Update personal cheat-sheet with monitoring panel links (shortcuts).
- Add automated test to CI that simulates replica lag and ensures alert fires.

End of shift checklist (to complete before handoff):
- [ ] Push blameless writeup draft to Confluence
- [x] Confirm redis cluster stable
- [x] Post incident summary in #incidents (short note + link to Confluence draft)
- [ ] File dashboard cleanup ticket
- [ ] Sync with Noah on ops PR status

Random notes / scratch (for later):
- Thought: quantify user impact in token-seconds lost during spike -> useful for post-mortem.
- Link to runbook we should standardize on: https://confluence.company/redwood-ops/oncall-runbook
- Slack refs: #sre-oncall, thread ts 1679145600.
